body:
## Summary

DES-015 incorrectly framed the server-side poller as a complete replacement for CronCreate. Other agents referencing this ADR get an incomplete picture of how autonomous inbox processing works.

The revised ADR documents the actual design: two cooperating layers.

| Layer | Owner | Mechanism | Purpose |
|-------|-------|-----------|---------|
| Detection | MCP server | Background goroutine + `tools/list_changed` | Detect new mail |
| Processing | Claude Code | Durable CronCreate `/inbox` | Read, archive, reply, flag |

`tools/list_changed` is a metadata signal — it updates tool descriptions but does not trigger the model to act. Without the CronCreate job, mail accumulates unprocessed. Tested 2026-04-12.

## Summary

- **Inspector test flake**: `test_inspect_brk_unblocks_after_debugger_connects` used fixed `sleep(500ms)` before sending `Debugger.resume`. On loaded CI runners, V8 might not be in the paused state yet, causing the resume to miss and the test to hang forever. Replaced with event-driven logic that waits for the `Debugger.paused` CDP event on the outbound channel before sending resume.

- **ConfigBridge shutdown hang**: `vtz ci build-typecheck` finished executing all tasks but the process hung indefinitely. The `ConfigBridge::shutdown()` method sends a shutdown JSON message to the JS loader but never closed stdin, so the `createInterface({ input: process.stdin })` readline kept the child process alive. Added `drop(self.stdin)` before `child.wait()` to send EOF.

author: ericmj
body:
## Summary

1xx informational responses (100 Continue, 103 Early Hints, etc.) were
bundled with `HEAD`/204/304 in `message_body/1`, so after parsing the 1xx
Mint emitted `{:done, ref}` and popped the request from the queue. The
real final response arriving afterwards had no active request and Mint
returned `{:error, %HTTPError{reason: {:unexpected_data, _}}}`, closing
the connection.

This broke two common scenarios:

- Requests sent with `Expect: 100-continue`, where the server sends 100
  Continue before the final response.
- Servers or intermediaries emitting unsolicited 1xx responses
  (`Plug.Conn.inform/3`, HAProxy 102 Processing, CDNs sending 103 Early
  Hints, etc.).

## Aligns HTTP/1 with the documented contract

`Mint.HTTP.stream/2` already documents the expected behavior for 1xx:

> `{:status, request_ref, status_code}` — You can have zero or more `1xx`
> `:status` and `:headers` responses for a single request, but they all
> precede a single non-`1xx` `:status` response.

HTTP/2 implements this (`lib/mint/http2.ex:1627-1659`, tested in
`test/mint/http2/conn_test.exs:989` under `describe "interim responses (1xx)"`),
but HTTP/1 did not — callers never saw the final `:status` because the
request was popped after the 1xx. This PR brings HTTP/1 behavior in line
with both the documented contract and the HTTP/2 implementation, so a
single handler works for both protocols.

## Fix

Split 1xx into a new `:informational` body kind in `message_body/1`. In
`decode_body/5`, the `:informational` clause resets the request's
response-side fields (`version`, `status`, `headers_buffer`, etc.) to
their initial state and continues parsing from `:status` without popping
the request. The `{:status, ref, 1xx}` and `{:headers, ref, _}` responses
are still emitted by the existing `:status`/`:headers` decode stages, so
informational responses remain visible to the caller; only the premature
`{:done, ref}` is suppressed.

## Summary

Changes from goal: v0.15.13.5 — Phase In-Progress Marking at Goal Start

**Why**: `ta run "..." --phase v0.x.y.z` starts the goal and creates the staging workspace, but PLAN.md still shows the phase as `pending` for the entire duration of the run. If another session adds a phase before the running one (or the user checks status mid-run), there's no signal that the phase is actively being worked. Fix: mark the phase `in_progress` in PLAN.md immediately when staging is created, before the agent launches.

**Impact**: 6 file(s) changed

## Changes (6 file(s))

- `~` `fs://workspace/PLAN.md` — Checked all 6 items in phase v0.15.13.5 as completed [x] with brief descriptions of what was implemented.
  - Phase tracking — all items are now implemented.
- `~` `fs://workspace/apps/ta-cli/src/commands/draft.rs` — In `deny_package()`, after the existing deny/memory/velocity logic, looks up the goal's `plan_phase` and calls `plan::reset_phase_if_in_progress`. Prints 'Plan: phase X reset to pending (goal denied)'. Added integration test `deny_package_resets_in_progress_phase_to_pending`.
  - Denial means the agent's work won't be applied. The phase must return to pending so the next attempt can mark it in_progress again and so `ta plan status` doesn't permanently show a denied goal's phase as in_progress.
- `~` `fs://workspace/apps/ta-cli/src/commands/goal.rs` — In `delete_goal()`, before removing staging/metadata, calls `plan::reset_phase_if_in_progress` with a note that includes the cancel reason. Added integration test `delete_goal_resets_in_progress_phase_to_pending`.
  - Deleting a goal ('ta goal delete') is the cancel path. The phase should return to pending so it's clear the work was abandoned and the phase is available to be re-started.
- `~` `fs://workspace/apps/ta-cli/src/commands/plan.rs` — Added two public helpers: `mark_phase_in_source(project_root, phase_id)` marks a pending phase in_progress and logs history; `reset_phase_if_in_progress(project_root, phase_id, note)` resets an in_progress phase to pending and logs history with a note. Updated `format_plan_checklist` and `format_plan_checklist_windowed` to show `[~]` for InProgress phases (was `[ ]`). Updated existing test that checked `[ ]` for an in_progress phase. Added 9 new tests covering mark/reset/noop/history/visual cases.

author: copilot
body:
DB errors during a poll cycle previously caused immediate application shutdown. Instead, `DataAccessException` should be logged and retried on the next schedule, with an option to silently suppress noise during idle periods.

## Changes

### `OutboxTableProperties` — two new config properties
- **`transientDbErrorSilenceAfterIdleMs`** (A): minimum idle duration (ms since last record read) before log suppression can activate. Default `0` = always log.
- **`transientDbErrorSilenceDurationMs`** (B): how long (ms) to suppress error logs once the idle threshold is met. Default `0` = always log.

Both default to `0` — fully backwards-compatible.

### `OutboxPollerRegistry` — split error handling
- `DataAccessException` is now caught separately: log (subject to suppression) and **retry**; no shutdown.
- All other exceptions (Kafka, etc.) remain **fatal** → `SpringApplication.exit` as before.
- Per-loop state tracks `lastRecordReadTimeMs` and `transientErrorFirstSeenMs` to drive the suppression decision:
  - suppress when idle ≥ A **and** current error run ≤ B
  - resets automatically on any cycle that completes without throwing
- New config values validated at startup (must be `>= 0`).

### Example configuration
```yaml
outbox:
  tables:
    - tableName: orders_outbox
      # after 5 min idle, silence transient DB errors for up to 2 min
      transientDbErrorSilenceAfterIdleMs: 300000   # A
      transientDbErrorSilenceDurationMs:  120000   # B
```

## Summary
This PR improves error handling across the application and ensures the `has_module_edit` function is properly defined in the database migrations and runtime setup.

- **Database & Migration Updates**
  - Added `has_module_edit()` function definition to both the SQL migration file and the `applyMigrations.ts` runtime setup to ensure it exists regardless of migration order

  - Updated TypeScript type from `Record<string, any>` to `Record<string, unknown>` for better type safety
  - Consistent error handling pattern: catch errors, log them, extract message if available, fall back to generic message

## Implementation Details
The error handling improvements follow a consistent pattern:
```typescript
catch (err) {
  console.error("Context:", err);
  const errorMsg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Unknown error";
  toast.error(errorMsg || "fallback message");
}
```

This ensures users see specific error messages when available while maintaining a fallback for unexpected error types.

### Motivation
- Failed dispatches were not visible in `/automacoes/logs` because workspace resolution used the wrong table, causing workspace_id mismatches between persistence and queries.
- Recipient and status values were inconsistently written/read, causing UI filters and rendering to miss real failures.
- Navigation back to `/automacoes` could hang on "Verificando acesso..." due to inconsistent application of the auth guard across the automations routes.

- Updated `lib/automation/get-workspace.js` to resolve the default workspace from `public.workspaces` (key=`default`) with a defensive fallback to the first active workspace, and adjusted resolver logging.
- Normalized logging in `lib/automation/log-dispatch.js` by canonicalizing status values (`success`/`error`/`failure`/`ignored` → `sent`/`failed`/`skipped`) and by normalizing/writing both `recipient` and `recipient_number` consistently.
- Hardened the logs API in `app/api/automation/logs/route.js` by normalizing incoming status filters and adding a diagnostic `console.info` containing the workspace, effective filters and returned count.
- Ensured consistent route protection for the automations module by adding `app/(admin)/automacoes/layout.js` that wraps the segment with `ProtectedRoute requiredRole="admin"` and removed the duplicate guard from `app/(admin)/automacoes/page.js`.
- Files changed: `lib/automation/get-workspace.js`, `lib/automation/log-dispatch.js`, `app/api/automation/logs/route.js`, `app/(admin)/automacoes/layout.js`, `app/(admin)/automacoes/page.js`.

- Replace the existing Vite/React TypeScript frontend with a lightweight PHP MVC backend to support a Full PHP + MySQL V1 migration strategy and simplify hosting on traditional PHP hosts. 
- Provide an operational, minimal CRM MVP backend (CRUD for prospects, notes, status, tags, sources) with server-rendered views so the product can run without the JS frontend. 
- Add documentation and migration guidance to capture the audit, migration plan and PHP setup for maintainers.

- Removes the Vite/React frontend and related Node tooling under `public/` (many `src` React files, `package.json`, `tsconfig`, `tailwind`, eslint and lockfiles were deleted) and adds PHP deployment helpers including `public/index.php`, `public/.htaccess`, `config/*.php`, `.env.example`, `PHP_BACKEND_SETUP.md`, `AUDIT.md`, and `MIGRATION_AUDIT.md`.
